headline: Steady growth persists as pay and deal costs squeeze margin
summary_short: Bentley's Q2 2026 revenue rose 12.8% y/y to $410.7M as ARR grew to $1.54B, while operating margin fell to 21.6% from 23.2% on higher deferred-comp and new integration costs. Diluted EPS still rose to $0.25 from $0.22, aided by a smaller share count and a net-other-income swing.
summary_long: Total revenue grew 12.8% y/y (12.2% constant currency) to $410.7M, led by the Resources sector and Public Works/Utilities; ARR reached $1,536.0M, up 11.4% y/y. Operating margin fell to 21.6% from 23.2% as deferred-compensation expense rose 53.8% y/y and a new $1.8M integration-cost adjustment began this quarter, partly offset by lower acquisition costs. Diluted EPS still rose to $0.25 from $0.22 on a 4.2% smaller share count and a swing to $15.6M of net other income. Cash rose to $147.0M as $264.9M of H1 operating cash flow and a $550M term loan covered $125.1M of buybacks and $677.8M of convertible-note repayments. No numeric full-year guidance change was given; management said results are tracking within its full-year outlook.

drivers.explanation: CFO cites constant-currency ARR growth of 12% and subscriptions growth of 13% as consistent, high performance within the full-year outlook, even as GAAP operating margin compressed on deferred-comp and new integration-cost adjustments; diluted EPS still rose on a smaller share count and non-operating gains.

CEO attributes growth to the Resources sector leading again, followed by Public Works/Utilities including the electric grid; reported growth (12.8%) modestly outpaced constant-currency growth (12.2%) on an FX tailwind this quarter versus a small headwind a year ago.

Not separately explained beyond the cost-of-revenue delta; gross margin expanded to 82.0% from 81.1% y/y as revenue growth (+12.8%) outpaced cost-of-revenue growth (+7.6%), while the q/q dip reflects a stronger Q1 cost base.

Margin fell to 21.6% from 23.2% as deferred-compensation plan expense rose to $11.7M from $7.6M and a new $1.8M integration-cost adjustment began this quarter per the non-GAAP reconciliation, partly offset by lower acquisition expenses ($2.4M vs $3.4M).

Not separately explained in the release; the y/y rise is consistent with a swing in 'Other income (expense), net' to +$15.6M from -$1.6M, partly offset by interest expense rising to $9.1M from $3.5M on higher debt.
Not separately explained in the release; tracks pretax income's y/y increase, partly offset by a higher tax provision ($16.6M vs $8.9M).

Six-month cash-flow statement shows $264.9M of operating cash flow plus $550M of new term-loan proceeds funded $677.8M of convertible-note repayments, $125.1M of buybacks, and $42.4M of dividends, for a net $23.7M rise in cash since December 2025.

Not separately explained in the release; the q/q rise is consistent with the $550M term loan drawn this quarter, while the y/y decline reflects $677.8M of convertible notes repaid over the trailing year outpacing new borrowing.

CFO cites 'a meaningful increase in share repurchases during the first half' as the cause; diluted share count fell 4.2% y/y and 0.9% q/q.
